expectations.text: Gives two completeness gates that are checkable before doors open and carry no numeric threshold
expectations.evidence: Gates table, pass/fail: on-duty visibility, cue-sheet completeness, handoff completeness.

expectations.text: Gate: every staffed post can name the organizer on duty for their block without asking anyone
expectations.evidence: 'Every staffed post names the on-duty organizer for their block, unprompted'.

expectations.text: Gate: every segment has a named owner, and every shift boundary has a handoff record with an entry or an explicit 'none' in each section
expectations.evidence: 'Every segment has a named owner'; 'Every shift boundary has a handoff record, with an entry or an explicit "none"'.

expectations.text: Labels the remaining metrics as ones this event sets for itself rather than benchmarks to hit
expectations.evidence: 'Every metric below is one you set, not a benchmark.'

expectations.text: Declines to supply an industry target number for dead air or transition adherence
expectations.evidence: 'There are no published targets... Target: none yet.'

expectations.text: Counts transition dead air separately at transitions the cue sheet scripted and transitions it did not
expectations.evidence: 'Count scripted transitions and unscripted ones separately.'

expectations.text: States that the scripted-versus-unscripted comparison is what justifies the depth choice next edition
expectations.evidence: 'if scripted transitions don't beat unscripted ones, the extra cue-sheet depth isn't paying off.'

expectations.text: Corrects the reading that zero escalations was a good sign, and states it usually means staff could not reach anyone
expectations.evidence: 'Zero escalations usually means staff could not reach anyone, not that nothing happened.'

expectations.text: Counts live changes made against the published disruption order separately from improvised ones, and names the improvised count as the one to drive down
expectations.evidence: 'count live changes made against the published disruption order versus improvised ones. The improvised number is the one to drive down'.

expectations.text: Tracks cue-sheet drift - rows that turned out wrong - as what a recurring edition's template inherits
expectations.evidence: 'rows that turned out wrong... go straight into next year's template.'

expectations.text: Tells the user to pick two or three metrics, write down the revision each would trigger, and record them before the day rather than after
expectations.evidence: 'pick these three'; 'Write the targets and the revision each metric triggers before the day.'

expectations.text: Captures what the document got wrong the same day rather than waiting for a later retrospective
expectations.evidence: 'Capture the numbers the same day. Cold retrospectives recover the decisions and lose the timings.'
